text: Isolate the tab component of request context by retaining only tab alongside user_id, video_id, weekday, and categorical hour.
rationale: The full request-context screen produced a positive training-only primary lift of 0.00221, but official diagnostics show severe weakness in tab 8 and tab 0, making a tab-only test informative about whether tab helps broadly or mainly introduces unstable sparse offsets.
exact_ablation: Remove hour and weekday from the current request-context feature set, retaining only categorical tab; keep the additive user/video scorer, BCE loss, optimizer, hyperparameters, split, and all other inputs unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small uncertain change, approximately -0.0015 to +0.0015; tab may provide within-user ordering signal, but the weak tab-8 GAUC of 0.352 and tab-0 GAUC of 0.541 indicate substantial heterogeneity.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small uncertain change, approximately -0.0020 to +0.0015; top-five quality could improve if tab separates relevant candidates, but sparse tabs may create harmful rank shifts.

text: Test weekday as the sole added request-context feature while removing tab and hour.
rationale: The request-context group is the only positively screened feature family, yet the prior cyclic-hour iteration showed no official primary movement. A weekday-only ablation separates stable calendar effects from the noisier intraday components without introducing rejected feature families.
exact_ablation: Replace the current tab, categorical/cyclic-hour, and weekday context block with weekday only; keep user_id, video_id, additive scoring, BCE training, and every training hyperparameter unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Near-zero to small increase, approximately -0.0005 to +0.0015, if weekday captures stable user ordering differences; the full screen's positive lift suggests some context value but does not identify weekday as the driver.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Near-zero change, approximately -0.0010 to +0.0015; weekday is shared across a user's candidates and may have limited ability to reorder top-five items.

text: Use categorical hour alone as the request-context addition, excluding tab and weekday.
rationale: Hour-specific diagnostics are weak at hour 3, 4, and 8, while later hours are stronger, so a focused categorical-hour test can determine whether the aggregate context lift is driven by hour despite heterogeneous support.
exact_ablation: Retain only categorical hour from the request-context block and remove tab, weekday, and cyclic-hour inputs; keep the additive user/video model, BCE loss, optimizer, and hyperparameters unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small uncertain change, approximately -0.0015 to +0.0015; hour can alter within-user ordering, but the hour-3 GAUC of 0.512 and hour-8 GAUC of 0.588 signal possible instability.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small uncertain change, approximately -0.0020 to +0.0015; hour may improve top-five ordering for some periods while hurting sparse-hour groups.

text: Replace the current hour representation with a continuous hour-and-minute phase encoding while retaining tab and weekday.
rationale: The current representation uses hour-level information, while the available feature inventory includes hourmin. A finer continuous phase could distinguish impressions within the same hour, especially where hour-level diagnostics are heterogeneous, without using post-impression data.
exact_ablation: Replace the current hour input with two normalized cyclic hour-minute features sin(2π·hourmin/1440) and cos(2π·hourmin/1440); retain tab, weekday, user_id, video_id, additive scoring, BCE, and all hyperparameters unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small uncertain increase, approximately -0.0010 to +0.0020; finer temporal resolution may recover within-hour ordering, but it may mostly add noise beyond the measured hour signal.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small uncertain increase, approximately -0.0015 to +0.0020; top-five ordering may benefit from finer context, with downside from overfitting sparse time regions.

text: Add a shallow nonlinear interaction branch to the existing additive scorer for user, video, tab, weekday, and hour features.
rationale: The current additive model cannot express that the same context affects different users or videos differently. The request-context screen has positive training-only evidence, while official tab and hour slices show heterogeneous performance consistent with conditional effects.
exact_ablation: Add one hidden layer of width 32 with ReLU over the existing encoded feature vector and concatenate its scalar output with the unchanged additive logit; change no feature values, loss, optimizer, batch size, or training schedule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small increase, approximately +0.0005 to +0.0030, if context effects are user/video conditional; overfitting could instead reduce GAUC by about 0.0015.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small increase, approximately +0.0005 to +0.0030, because nonlinear context interactions may correct top-five ordering; rare tab groups remain a downside risk.

text: Add a bounded-order cross branch over the existing encoded user, video, tab, weekday, and hour features.
rationale: A cross branch directly targets conditional interactions such as user-by-tab or video-by-hour, which the additive scorer cannot represent. This is motivated by the positive request-context screen and the large diagnostic spread across tabs and hours.
exact_ablation: Add exactly two low-rank cross layers over the existing encoded feature vector, concatenate the cross output with the unchanged additive logit, and keep features, BCE loss, optimizer, batch size, and stopping schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small possible increase, approximately +0.0005 to +0.0035, if bounded interactions improve candidate ordering; memorization of sparse tab-hour combinations could reduce GAUC by up to 0.0020.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small possible increase, approximately +0.0005 to +0.0035, with greater upside than GAUC if conditional crosses repair top ranks; rare-context overfitting is the main downside.

text: Change only the pointwise BCE objective to a within-user pairwise logistic ranking loss.
rationale: The official objective is ranking-based, and the current BCE model reaches GAUC 0.66937 and nDCG@5 0.53667. A pairwise loss may focus updates on positive-negative ordering rather than calibration, although the two official metrics can move differently.
exact_ablation: Replace BCE with a within-user pairwise logistic loss over sampled positive-negative impression pairs; keep the current features, additive model, optimizer, batch budget, sampling seed, and evaluation artifact contract unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Moderate possible increase, approximately +0.0010 to +0.0040, because the loss directly optimizes positive-negative ordering; noisy or unbalanced pair sampling could instead lower GAUC by 0.0020.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small uncertain increase, approximately -0.0010 to +0.0030; pairwise separation may improve top ranks, but it does not explicitly weight the first five positions.

text: Change only the pointwise BCE objective to a within-user listwise softmax loss over each displayed user group.
rationale: nDCG@5 is sensitive to top-of-list placement, whereas BCE treats rows independently. A listwise objective may better coordinate scores within each displayed user group, with the risk that small or single-positive groups dominate optimization.
exact_ablation: Replace BCE with a groupwise softmax cross-entropy over each user's displayed impression group using long_view relevance as the target distribution; retain the same features, additive scorer, optimizer, number of training epochs, and all preprocessing.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small uncertain change, approximately -0.0010 to +0.0030; coordinated group training may improve ordering but can sacrifice broad pairwise separation.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Moderate possible increase, approximately +0.0010 to +0.0040, because the loss emphasizes relative placement within groups; groups with one positive may create unstable gradients.

text: Use a top-five-weighted pairwise ranking loss that upweights positive-negative pairs involving the current predicted top five.
rationale: The current model has materially weak top-five quality in tab 8 and tab 0 despite the aggregate nDCG@5 of 0.53667. A rank-focused loss targets the metric component most likely to be under-optimized, but can harm GAUC below rank five.
exact_ablation: Replace BCE with a pairwise loss whose pair weight is 2 for pairs involving a current predicted top-five row and 1 otherwise; keep the model, feature set, optimizer, batch budget, and all sampling rules unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small uncertain change, approximately -0.0020 to +0.0020; concentrating updates near the top can improve useful pairs but may reduce ordering quality elsewhere.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small possible increase, approximately +0.0010 to +0.0040, if top-five mistakes are corrected; unstable top-five membership early in training is a downside risk.

text: Replace uniform row sampling during training with user-group-balanced minibatches while keeping BCE unchanged.
rationale: The official metrics evaluate within-user ranking, while the current training loop samples rows uniformly. Balancing users could provide more consistent group-level learning, but may distort the natural impression distribution and trade GAUC against nDCG@5.
exact_ablation: Change only minibatch construction so each batch contains an equal number of sampled users with their available training rows; retain BCE, the current feature set, additive scorer, learning rate, epochs, and evaluation distribution unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small possible increase, approximately +0.0005 to +0.0030, if underrepresented users receive more useful updates; oversampling tiny users could reduce positive-count-weighted GAUC by about 0.0020.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small uncertain increase, approximately -0.0010 to +0.0030; better user coverage may help macro top-five quality, but distribution shift in training can hurt frequent-user ranking.

text: Add deterministic temporal decay to the BCE training weights so recent training impressions receive higher weight.
rationale: The request-context screen's daily primary lift rose from 0.00067 on 20220418 to 0.00870 on 20220421, suggesting temporal nonstationarity. Recency weighting could prioritize patterns closer to validation, but can increase variance and overfit the latest days.
exact_ablation: Multiply each training-row BCE loss by a fixed linear time-decay weight ranging from 0.5 on the earliest training date to 1.0 on the latest training date, normalized to preserve mean weight; change nothing else.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small possible increase, approximately +0.0005 to +0.0030, if recent context patterns persist into validation; temporal overfitting could lower GAUC by 0.0020.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small uncertain increase, approximately -0.0010 to +0.0030; fresher patterns may improve top-five ordering, while long-tail users and items may lose support.

text: Increase only L2 regularization on the existing additive context model to reduce sparse-context overfitting.
rationale: Official diagnostics show very weak sparse context cells, especially tab 8 with nDCG@5 0.026 and tab 0 with nDCG@5 0.062, while the full model's aggregate metrics remain moderate. Stronger regularization is a clean non-feature intervention that may stabilize rare tab and hour offsets.
exact_ablation: Change only L2 from 1e-6 to 1e-4 for all additive weights; retain the current user/video/tab/weekday/hour features, BCE objective, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and stopping rule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small uncertain change, approximately -0.0010 to +0.0020; shrinkage may improve rare-context generalization but can weaken useful user/video separation.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small possible increase, approximately -0.0010 to +0.0025, if extreme sparse offsets currently displace good candidates; excessive shrinkage may flatten top-five scores.
